title: Assign Tennis Bookings to Courts
prompt:
A tennis club receives a list of bookings, each with a start and finish time. There is no fixed limit on courts. Return a plan assigning every booking to one court so that no court has overlapping bookings, using as few courts as possible.

**Part 1.** Implement `assign_courts(bookings, maintenance=0) -> list[int]`. Return the court ID for each booking in its original input order. Court IDs are consecutive integers starting at 0; any valid minimum-court plan is accepted. The input may be unsorted and must not be modified.

**Part 2.** A court now needs `maintenance` units of time after each booking. Extend your solution so the next booking on that court starts at or after `finish + maintenance`.

Practice agreement: bookings are integer pairs `(start, finish)` with `start < finish`; maintenance is a nonnegative integer. Intervals are half-open, so a court is reusable exactly at its release time. Empty input returns `[]`.

| Bookings | Maintenance | One optimal plan |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[(0, 10), (5, 7), (10, 12)]` | `0` | `[0, 1, 0]` |
| `[(0, 10), (5, 7), (10, 12)]` | `3` | `[0, 1, 1]` |

Explain why your plan uses the minimum number of courts and give its time and space complexity.
background_note: The original MLE report asks for a minimum-court assignment and maintenance after a booking. The function signature, integer representation, original-order output, half-open equality rule and consecutive IDs are local executable conventions. No particular assignment or tie-break is required. A third maintenance-by-accumulated-usage stage from secondary preparation pages was not established by these original reports and is not required.

example.reasoning: The first two bookings overlap. The third can reuse a court at time 10.
